significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish both a phenomenon and mechanism: cross-language divergence in answers to culturally underspecified questions is predictable from cultural distance, while a compact residual-stream “cultural context” direction causally controls that divergence and is “largely separate from factual-knowledge subspaces.” This includes a form-(iii) predictive coupling between cultural distance and default divergence, plus a form-(ii) causal decomposition that fixes expectations across languages and explains why otherwise equivalent prompts elicit different defaults; this would connect behavioral concerns documented by Naous et al. (2024), “Having Beer after Prayer?,” with the shared-versus-language-specific internal processing studied by Wendler et al. (2024), “Do Llamas Work in English?” The branches are distinguishable and informative: failure of the behavioral relation supports a common or monocultural default, while behavior without the compact separable direction rules out that particular mechanistic explanation, although rejection of the composite claim would not by itself identify which component failed. In the topic-substitution self-check, multilingual representation alone would not earn this score: the specific cultural-distance law and separable causal mechanism are more constraining than the median shared-versus-language-specific hypothesis.

reach.justification: The claim names two reusable handles: the measurable “Cultural-Default-Alignment” relation and an intervention where “steering this direction lets a query in one language yield answers grounded in a chosen alternative cultural context.” The steering handle is ex ante because it changes the cultural grounding during generation, leaving an action window for localization or deployment, while the alignment measure can audit defaults before a model is shipped; likely downstream users therefore include model auditors and localization practitioners, not only mechanistic-interpretability researchers. After per-model re-extraction, the exact direction would be rediscovered rather than numerically transferred, but the asserted relation that default divergence scales with cultural distance predicts what should recur across model families, languages, and cultural-question domains. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic multilingual-transfer research supplies neither this specific auditing quantity nor an on-demand cultural-context control handle.
